title: Hours, price, limit
description: How many client hours you really have, what an hour is worth once you count the work outside sessions, how your cycle works, and where one-to-one work ends in money and strength.

units.title: Hours and the price of an hour

objectives.text: Work out the price of every working hour, not only of a session
Describe your cycle: its length, frequency, and the rules for rescheduling and cancelling
Find your limit of hours per week and the ceiling of income at your current price

checks.question: 20 sessions a week at 60 each, plus 8 more hours of work outside sessions. What is the price of a working hour?
checks.explain: The revenue of the week is 20 × 60 = 1200. Working hours: 20 + 8 = 28. 1200 ÷ 28 ≈ 43 (u1, worked example).

checks.question: Of 20 sessions at 60, two were cancelled without payment. How much was lost in the week?
options: Nothing: the sessions will be moved
checks.explain: Two sessions at 60 are 120 of 1200, minus 10 percent. Until a cancellation rule is named, such losses are invisible (u2, “Rescheduling and cancellations”).

checks.question: The limit is 22 client hours a week, the price of a session is 60. What is the ceiling of the week?
options: There is no ceiling: you can raise the price
checks.explain: The ceiling of the week = limit × price: 22 × 60 = 1320. You can raise the price, but it has a limit too: some clients start coming less often (u3, “The ceiling of the week”).
